correctness.rationale: For all six coefficients of modulus exactly one, normalization c00=c10=c01=1 is a unique action by common, horizontal and vertical phases. Write P=A+wB, A=1+z+exp(iv)z^2, B=1+exp(iu)z+exp(it)z^2. Orthogonality gives M=58+2(|1+exp(iv)|^2+|exp(iu)+exp(i(t-u))|^2) +8 Re[(1+exp(iv))*conj(exp(iu)+exp(i(t-u)))+exp(i(v-t))]. For x=cos(v/2), y=cos(u-t/2), z0=cos((v-t)/2), exact algebra gives M-50=8[2(z0+xy)^2+x^2(1-y^2)+y^2(1-x^2)]>=0. Equality x=y=z0=0 yields two normalized representatives (1,1,-1 ; 1,+/-i,1); equality |x|=|y|=1, z0=-xy yields (1,1,1 ; 1,-1,1), no others. For rectangular support S, M=sum_h|R(h)|^2 <=sum_h|S intersect (S+h)|^2=19*6=114. Equality in nearest horizontal and vertical shifts forces all adjacent phase ratios constant, hence coefficients lambda*alpha^i*beta^j; such arrays attain 114. Continuity of M on connected T^6 gives every intermediate moment. M-36=14 at minimum, giving merit factor 18/7. Discrete q-phase orbits have exactly q^3 representatives per normalized pattern, with type I available iff 2|q and both II patterns iff 4|q; 8 binary/192 quaternary minima. A compact abelian group with 15 distinct chi^r eta^s frequencies for P^2 has identical convolution Parseval; m>=5,n>=3 grids satisfy this. Independent aperiodic autocorrelation evaluation reproduced 50 for each minimizing representative and 114 for affine-phase all ones; complete q=2 (64 arrays: energies 50:8,58:32,66:16,114:8) and q=4 (4096 arrays: min50 count192, max114 count64) corroborated. Direct angle substitutions reproduced the exact global sum-of-squares identity (sample continuous values 53.0168880975 and 113.6209155619). These finite tests are supplementary; the continuous/all-q/general-group statements depend on the analytic arguments.

value.rationale: Full 3-by-2 Cartesian aperture is a naturally motivated small two-dimensional array having multiple overlapping horizontal shifts and cross-row correlations; the full aperiodic squared sidelobe energy and merit factor are standard design invariants. The unrestricted complex-phase global minimum and exactly three phase-modulation orbit types give a structural, closed classification rather than a random slice or a finite binary lookup. The even-q attainability and q^3 versus 3q^3 exact counts distinguish real sign and quadrature phase cancellations. A future optimization or small-array classification can use these exact signatures as a base case/benchmark. The result neither establishes higher-dimensional array-optimality nor claims novelty for the classical binary optimum or easy upper bound; its value is the complete previously unlocated continuous-phase equality classification.
